To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed methods of weighting the entities of a knowledge graph improve its performance in the task of semantic parsing and relation detection.

(1) the use of semantic graph entities and relations for relation detection in semantic parsing is beneficial; (2) the use of weights for entities and relations improves the performance of relation detection in semantic interpretation; and (3) weights for entities and their relations can be derived from knowledge graphs, Wikipedia documents and user queries.

(1) using weighted semantic graphs can improve the performance of relation detection in conversations, and (2) the weights can be derived from real world data, such as the usage frequencies of entities in user queries, and (3) the weights can also be derived from the knowledge graph itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to enrich knowledge graphs for relation detection in the context of conversational understanding.
the following questions: How can we assign probabilistic weights to entities in semantic graphs? How do such weights benefit relation detection in conversual understanding?
